findings.location: lib/core/sync/sync_engine.dart:140-151 (`_flush`'s `for (final answer in pending)` loop); lib/core/sync/media_upload_coordinator.dart:112-119 (`scanAll`'s `for (final row in rows)` loop)
findings.evidence: Both loops now re-check `_backoff.isActive` immediately after each row/answer and `break` as soon as it becomes true: `sync_engine.dart` lines 150-151 (`if (_backoff.isActive) break;` right after `flushedAny = true;`) and `media_upload_coordinator.dart` lines 115-118 (`if (_backoff.isActive) break;` right after `await _advance(row);`). A 429 hit on any row now stops the rest of that same pass rather than letting every remaining row also fire and re-register/compound the backoff.
findings.why_it_matters: Confirmed fixed — a 429 partway through a pass now stops all remaining rows in that pass, matching phase-07's Design Constraint (b) that the backoff must suppress the entire flush/scan pass, not just the offending row.

findings.evidence: The shared teardown is now extracted into a single private method `_completeAttempt(String attemptPublicId, Emitter<ExamAttemptState> emit)` (lines 161-168) containing `_attemptPublicId = null`, `_syncEngine.setActiveTask(null)`, `_syncEngine.stopSync()`, `_timerService.stop()`, `_mediaUploadCoordinator.stop()`, and `emit(AttemptCompleted(attemptPublicId))`. Both `_onForceSubmitRequested` (line 151, after a successful `forceSubmit`) and `_emitFromResponse` (line 172, when `response.completed`) call this one method — no duplication remains.
findings.why_it_matters: Confirmed fixed — the two 'same outcome' paths this phase's contract requires to stay identical now share one implementation, eliminating the drift risk.
